purpose: Unapproved visual composition proposals only; not production assets
A:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: Visual DESIGN PROPOSAL board for MemoryGarden, not production art, not a functioning app screenshot. The viewer is choosing the composition before implementation.
Reference images: Image 1 is the existing garden's watercolor/gouache ART STYLE and warm lighting reference only; completely recompose its layout as specified. Image 2 is the existing sunflower's botanical illustration style and proportions. Do not imitate a photograph. Preserve the mature, cozy, hand-painted storybook direction.
Board layout: polished landscape 3:2 presentation board on a slim cream surround. A large desktop populated-garden view occupies the upper-left 70% (roughly 1000x560). A tall mobile portrait view occupies the right 27% (roughly 350x750). Two smaller landscape views sit below the main desktop view: the SAME garden empty at first visit, then the SAME garden dimmed with an open botanical journal. Small understated board labels outside the views: "Desktop garden", "First visit", "Journal", "Mobile". Make the actual in-app views visually prominent and coherent, not a wireframe or collage of stock photos.
Within EVERY application view: the illustrated garden fills the entire view edge to edge. NO website header band, footer band, hero heading, panels, dashboard cards, debug controls, counters, sidebars, browser chrome, phone hardware frame, or replay button. Tiny "MemoryGarden" identity upper-left on an unobtrusive cream tag/wood plaque. Only two small touch-friendly controls upper-right: journal icon and garden-page arrows. The ONE discoverable primary action is "Plant a Memory" on an illustrated journal/seed-packet ribbon at the lower edge integrated with scenery, without a full-width bar. Keep all controls inset and readable.
Garden semantics: about ten intentional planting locations in organically shaped earth beds, not a grid or glowing sci-fi dots. Show subtle shallow soil nests in empty spots, each with enough space for an individual flower. The first spot gets one small wooden sign "Your story begins here". Populated desktop and mobile show just three planted sunflowers at separate intended roots, varied gently for depth, with believable soil contact, restrained contact shadow and foreground grass overlapping only the lowest stem. Remaining spots stay empty. No giant standalone flower pasted above grass. Do NOT draw or develop the complete six-flower asset collection.
Journal inset: same garden softly dimmed behind a warm cream two-page botanical journal with thin botanical margins and real-looking typeset text. Left page prompt "What moment would you like to remember?" with spacious writing lines, subtle date/photo controls. Right page botanical illustration and discreet "Find My Flower" / "Choose manually". This is a future JOURNAL DESIGN MOCKUP only. It must feel part of the world, not a conventional web form.
The portrait view MUST be an intentional recomposition of the SAME garden, with its planting beds and ten logical spots still visible and usable, all controls readable. Do not squeeze a wide screenshot into a portrait frame. Natural layered foreground, midground and background. Soft sage/olive greens, cream, muted gold light from upper left, hand-painted brush detail, quiet whimsy for young adults. Clear focal planting areas. No characters, avatar, navigation movement, 3D, pixel art, realistic photography, animals dominating, watermarks or large marketing text.
DIRECTION A — "The Secret Glade": an intimate, enclosed single-level garden clearing seen from an elevated three-quarter perspective. Arrange TWO broad horseshoe-shaped planting beds around a SMALL curved stepping-stone loop, leaving open grass between the beds. The pathways should lead the eye around plantable areas, not consume the middle as a road. Four planting nests in one bed, six in the other, with generous organic spacing and no regimented rows. The trees, low wooden fence and flowering hedge embrace the scene at the back. A few larger foreground leaves and soft grasses frame the lower corners to make the viewer feel INSIDE a little garden. Midground sunflowers sit among garden beds, modestly scaled to the decorative plants. The lower-right foreground contains a small closed botanical journal with a pale cloth bookmark labeled "Plant a Memory", visually an invitation to open the book; do not introduce a big table or toolbar. On mobile recompose the two curving beds around a narrower S-shaped path while preserving all ten logical spots. Keep the opening garden beautiful and inviting with NO planted-memory flowers in the First visit inset. The journal inset opens from that book, keeping the garden visible around it.

DIRECTION B — "The Terraced Story Garden": a distinct stepped miniature garden, elevated three-quarter view with stronger depth than a flat clearing. A short diagonal stepping-stone stair runs from lower-left toward an upper-right back gate. THREE broad gently curved planting terraces (low natural stone retaining edges, not raised rectangular planters) create clear foreground/middle/background shelves for ten memory roots: four in front, three in middle, three in back. Flowers at the back are smaller, with larger front flowers; all ten positions remain separate and readable. A soft canopy and old fence enclose the background, grasses overlap the bases of stone edges in front. Restrained stone textures should be hand-painted, never photoreal. Keep the shelves broad and accessible, not a complicated landscape or open world. The primary "Plant a Memory" action is a warm illustrated seed packet with a small journal emblem nestled by the lower-left path entrance, not a website button bar. Tiny "MemoryGarden" identity is an engraved wooden tag upper-left. Mobile re-blocks the same ten logical roots into vertically staggered terraces with a clear winding stair, never a crop that loses a terrace. Empty first-visit view contains shaped earth nests without memory flowers. The journal inset rises from the seed-packet/book action and opens above this terraced garden; on mobile the future journal will be a single readable page.
